_threat_model: This agent is triggered by whatever PDF lands in the Dropbox inbox. A research PDF is
ATTACKER-CONTROLLED INPUT: it can carry text aimed at an AI reader. The agent runs unattended,
so nobody is watching when it does.
READ THIS BEFORE WIDENING ANYTHING — two properties make an allow-list here weaker than it looks:
1. --settings is ADDITIVE, NOT REPLACING. `claude --help`: 'load ADDITIONAL settings from'.
The watcher runs with cwd = the repo, so .claude/settings.local.json loads TOO — 124 allow
entries with no deny section. Verified by differential test: `conda info --envs` RAN with
cwd=repo and was BLOCKED with cwd=elsewhere, same --settings flag. This file therefore
cannot restrict by omission. Only the deny list below actually binds, because deny wins.
2. A GENERAL-PURPOSE INTERPRETER IS A UNIVERSAL BYPASS. `Bash(python3:*)` was previously in the
allow list here; python opens sockets, writes anywhere, and spawns processes, which defeats
every network and filesystem denial in one line. Verified: python3 -c 'print(6*7)' ran
unattended under the old settings. Interpreters are now explicitly DENIED.
The deny list is the boundary. Treat additions to it as load-bearing and additions to the allow
list as convenience only. This is defence in depth, NOT a sandbox — the honest containment story
is that the digest touches only the reports library and cannot reach the network.
NOTE: deny rules for file writes must use Edit(<path>) — Write(<path>) is silently a no-op; Claude Code matches all file-editing tools on Edit rules. Verified: it warns at startup.
